Surge by Peak XV FAQs | Funding, Eligibility, Applications & Evaluation Startups How we partner People Resources Apply FAQs About Surge What is Surge? Surge is how Peak XV backs founders from day zero. We started Surge in 2019 with a simple goal: help early-stage founders build strong foundations for an enduring company. Since then, we've partnered with 400+ founders building in diverse sectors across the globe, from first check through their scale. Alongside capital, you get hands-on support from the Surge team across hiring, GTM, product, fundraising and more - with operators who've seen the playbook and are in your corner to run it with you. Once a year, we also bring the cohort together for an 8-week Immersion - time with the world's most iconic founders and operators, focused sector tracks, and a founder community that sticks around for life. How much funding will my startup receive? Surge invests up to $5 million in seed capital in each company through an equity investment. Our investments range from $500-$5M. How will the Surge team and community help me build my company? Founders will work with Surge team members, mentors, and experts to make tangible progress towards launching or accelerating their companies. Each company has a dedicated investment advisor who will work with you to define actionable 16-week goals. The team will guide you to lay down the overall
The team will guide you to lay down the overall strategy, track weekly progress, and connect you to mentors and experts.
Build networks, find mentors and form friendships that will stay with you forever.
Early-stage journeys evolve, pivots happen, and that’s exactly why it helps to start the conversation sooner.
We work with founders at the idea stage as well, long before things are set in stone.
Surge is the way Peak XV does seed investing.
Founders receive up to $5M in seed capital, along with access to Peak XV’s network, operating expertise and long-term follow-on support as they scale.
I’ve already been to an accelerator, what do I get out of this program?
The standard accelerator model is often 12–24 week building window with support ending at demo day.
Surge does not take board seats at the early stage.

This 8-week journey wraps with an Immersion in San Francisco with other early-stage founders in the Peak XV community, and curated visits to iconic companies like NVIDIA, OpenAI, Google, Notion.

Surge 12 | Building the next era of AI, deeptech, consumer and fintech Startups How we partner People Resources Apply ← Back Surge 12 Building the next era of AI, deeptech, consumer and fintech Social media copy AUTHOR Surge Team We’re excited to welcome 18 new companies to Surge 12 , building across AI, robotics, space, consumer, healthcare, music and fintech. Every Surge cohort gives us a window into what ambitious early-stage founders are choosing to build right now. With Surge 12, three shifts stood out to us. Familiar consumer behaviours are being rebuilt around new expectations. AI is moving from a feature to the underlying architecture of products. And technology is increasingly leaving the screen to tackle physical infrastructure and the real world. Across all three, there’s a common instinct: start from first principles. Our Surge founders are asking whether the products and systems we’ve grown accustomed to should work the way they do at all, and what they might look like if they were being built from scratch today. Rebuilding familiar behaviours Some of the companies in Surge 12 are taking experiences we already know well and rethinking how they should work. August AI is building autonomous clinical intelligence for primary care, combining AI with physician-led care. The company has already grown to nine million users across 160 countries. Ditto is moving dating
Ditto is moving dating beyond endless swiping, while Wingit is building a beauty platform for India’s premium consumers.
GameStock is applying the mechanics of competition to financial markets, and Hoola Health is building a child-first paediatric care ecosystem.
And Tribe Money wants to put personal finances on autopilot, using AI to manage the tracking, research and investing decisions that often fall through the cracks.
AI is becoming the architecture AI runs through much of Surge 12, but increasingly not as a standalone product or feature.
Alma is rethinking personal computing for an AI-native world.
Rosella is redesigning commercial insurance brokerage around AI, while Kindling is building a storytelling operating system for ambitious tech startups.
Reinforce Labs is building the evaluation, red-teaming and remediation layer for enterprise AI, helping teams make AI systems safer and more reliable in production.
And hiloop is building infrastructure for post-training open-weight models, a research harness that helps application-layer AI companies run, track and improve model experiments at scale.
Together, these companies reflect a shift we think is becoming increasingly important: AI is moving from being the product itself to becoming part of how the product fundamentally works.

From robotics beneath our cities to sensing systems above the Earth, these founders are showing how advances in hardware, software and AI are opening up entirely new categories of problems for startups to tackle.
Anish Das Sarma , founder of Reinforce Labs, completed a PhD at Stanford, built a company that was acquired by Airbnb and later led AI and machine-learning teams as a Director at Google.
Nischith Shadagopan M N and Vinod Ganesan , founders of Alma, previously worked together at Microsoft Research and became founding engineers at Sarvam AI.

That journey continues with Surge 11, our newest cohort. On September 25, founders from 23 startups came together in Mumbai to kick off the program This group of ambitious doers and dreamers showcases a remarkable range of sectors: 12 AI startups across consumer, enterprise, and vertical markets; four fintech innovators; four consumer brands; and three infrastructure and developer tools companies. What unites these founders is grit, the courage to tackle tough challenges, and a first-principles mindset. Surge 11 is also special for its eclectic mix, including many second-time founders, a legendary cricketer, and an Olympic swimming medallist. Together, this cohort is reinventing what’s next for consumers, developers, and enterprises across India, APAC, and global markets. Our three-day kickoff included Fireside Chats where leaders like Amrish Rau, Ronnie Screwvala, Adwaita Nayar, and Dheeraj Pandey spoke about what it takes to build an enduring company. Surge founders also heard from legends Sachin Tendulkar and Usain Bolt about the great rewards that come from resilience and discipline. The event brought together founders from past cohorts

Special shout-out to the amazing leaders of our Founder Circles who came to pay it forward by sharing their journeys: Kaushik Mudda (Ethereal Machines): Building a manufacturing powerhouse from India against all odds.
Gaurav Baheti (Procol): On landing the first big enterprise win.
Varun Banka (Atlan): Winning Fortune 500 with product excellence.
Vinay Maheshwari (The Health Factory): Scaling 100x on quick commerce.
Shiva Dhawan & Rishabjit Singh (Attentive): Building AI products from the ground up.
Saurabh Arora (Plum): Reinventing the org with AI across functions.
